QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the constant external pressure required to expand 2 moles of an ideal gas from volume 15 dm³ to 20 dm³ if amount of work done is -600 J.

Solution.S:
Given: $V_1 = 15$ dm³, $V_2 = 20$ dm³, $w = -600$ J, $n = 2$ mol.

$\Delta V = V_2 - V_1 = 20 - 15 = 5$ dm³ = $5 \times 10^{-3}$ m³.

Work done at constant external pressure:
$$w = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$$

Substitute values:
$$-600 = -P_{\text{ext}} \times (5 \times 10^{-3})$$

$$600 = P_{\text{ext}} \times 5 \times 10^{-3}$$

$$P_{\text{ext}} = \frac{600}{5 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{600}{0.005} = 120000 \text{ Pa}$$

Convert to bar ($1$ bar = $10^5$ Pa):
$$P_{\text{ext}} = \frac{120000}{100000} = 1.2 \text{ bar}$$

Thus the correct option is A: 1.2 bar.
